text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Vietnam has agreed with other members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations that the use of Vietnam's existing rail network would save money and time for the development of a Trans-Asia rail-link.
-- Denmark has weighed in behind the World Bank with a donation of $10 million to assist a scheme to reform and develop Vietnam's national economic structure.

-- Tenders were due to be called on Sunday for a $17-million project to upgrade the control centre for the southern provinces' electricity network. The World Bank will provide $14 million for an Energy Management System for the control centre, which is to be equipped with Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet told reporters that infrastructure development was Vietnam's top priority in its contribution in the development of the Mekong river sub-region.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has called on the Party and state to pay attention to the aspirations of Vietnamese writers and ensure freedom and democracy in the field of literatura.
-- Do Quoc Sam, former minister of planning and investment, has been appointed head of the State Evaluation Commission for investment projects.
